title: Low-Rank Few-Shot Node Classification by Node-Level Graph Diffusion
claim: Adding more synthetic samples eventually hurts accuracy due to noise, but adding a regularizer keeps performance high and stable.
layout: 1 panel line plot, two series, accuracy versus synthetic-support multiplier
description: A single line chart with a dashed grid. The x-axis shows the number of synthetic support nodes as a multiple of the original support set, from 0 to 10. The y-axis shows accuracy in percent, from 80 to 90. A blue line with square markers, labeled COLA (FGDM), rises from about 87.8 to a peak near 88.7 at 3x. It then falls steadily to about 83.4 at 10x. A coral line with diamond markers, labeled COLA (LR-FGDM), rises from about 88.2 to about 89.6 at 4x. It declines only slightly to about 87.9 at 10x. The coral line stays above the blue line everywhere. The gap widens sharply at high augmentation levels. A legend box sits in the lower right. The eye goes first to the diverging curves on the right.
caption: 5-way 5-shot node classification accuracies on CoraFull trained with different numbers of synthetic support nodes added. COLA (LR-FGDM) is trained on the augmented graph by FGDM with the low-rank regularization, while COLA (FGDM) is trained without the regularization.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel node-level graph diffusion method with low-rank feature learning for few-shot node classification (FSNC), termed Low-Rank Few-Shot Graph Diffusion Model or LR-FGDM. LR-FGDM first employs a novel Few-Shot Graph Diffusion Model (FGDM) as a node-level graph generative method to generate an augmented graph with an enlarged support set, then performs low-rank transductive classification to obtain the few-shot node classification results. Our graph diffusion model, FGDM, comprises two components, the Hierarchical Graph Autoencoder (HGAE) with an efficient hierarchical edge reconstruction method and a new prototypical regularization, and the Latent Diffusion Model (LDM). The low-rank regularization is robust to the noise inherently introduced by the diffusion model and empirically inspired by the Low Frequency Property. We also provide a strong theoretical guarantee justifying the low-rank regularization for the transductive classification in few-shot learning. To further enhance the performance of LR-FGDM, we introduce LRA-LR-FGDM with a novel efficient LR-Attention layer, or the LRA layer, which applies self-attention to the output of the LR-FGDM encoder. The LRA layer further reduces the kernel complexity of LR-FGDM and contributes to a tighter generalization bound, leading to improved performance. Extensive experimental results evidence the effectiveness of LR-FGDM for few-shot node classification, which outperforms the current state-of-the-art. The code of the LR-FGDM is available at \url{https://github.com/Statistical-Deep-Learning/LR-FGDM}.
